survey.question: Which thread should I watch more closely this week?

items.title: Josh Downs' first day as a Chief: he'll wear No. 12, and KC waived returner Nikko Remigio and rookie DE Jack Pyburn to clear room
items.subheader: Downs called it a blessing to play alongside Mahomes and said he'd heard Reid is a 'great mastermind of offense.' On the number: he wore 1 and then 2, so the equipment manager told him to put them together.
items.image_alt: Josh Downs meets the Kansas City media

quotes.text: It's good when guys welcome you and accept you. I feel like at this point it's my turn to earn their respect on the field, and earn their respect as a teammate. I'm going to do what I can to do that.

items.title: The chemistry head start: Rashee Rice says he and Downs have trained together every offseason since before the draft
items.subheader: Rice texted Downs eye emojis the night of the trade; the two share a locker-room area and have been walking through the playbook together. Downs called Rice 'my dog' and said the relationship factored into wanting KC.
items.image_alt: Josh Downs in his No. 12 Chiefs jersey at the podium

quotes.text: I train with Josh in the offseason, as well as coming out of college. So, we've had a relationship prior. We're in the same area in the locker room, so we're in there joking around.

items.title: Wednesday practice: Mahomes (elbow), Rice (knee) and Worthy (hamstring) were all full participants; Downs isn't on the injury report at all
items.subheader: Two days after Reid called all three day-to-day, the full-practice tags point to Mahomes and his top three receivers being available Sunday in Atlanta.

items.title: Wednesday availability report: LB Owen Chambliss and CB Andrew Marshall are out for Rutgers; Rutgers star WR KJ Duff's season is over after ankle surgery
items.subheader: Chambliss (55 tackles, an INT) is the country's No. 27-graded linebacker per Pro Football Network; Marshall is its No. 17 corner. Vincent Shavers, Dexter Foster and Dawson Merritt are next up at linebacker. Rutgers backup QB AJ Surace is expected to start.
items.image_alt: Owen Chambliss and KJ Duff, both out Saturday

items.title: Why Saturday matters beyond bowl math: Nebraska is 7-0 all-time against Rutgers (184-96 scoring), but the last three meetings were one-score games
items.subheader: A sixth win guarantees a non-losing regular season after the Huskers averaged 13.5 points during the four-game skid. SI notes the fair question already being asked: if Nebraska loses out to finish 5-7, does Rhule survive a contract that runs through 2032?
items.image_alt: Anthony Colandrea's 39-yard touchdown run against Indiana

items.title: Antigravity is rolling out browser use: agents can now run and verify the code they write in a live browser, with auth and downloads gated on your approval
items.subheader: The /browser command closes the research-code-verify loop - playtest a checkout flow, check a mobile viewport, report console errors. Users control authentication, downloads pause for approval, and agents can run multiple browser tasks in parallel.

items.title: DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 predicts how DNA variants change specific cell types - and doubles variant identification over the original
items.subheader: The model adapts to new cell states without retraining and pinpoints disease-relevant mutations in primary human cells. Available now for non-commercial use.

items.title: OpenRouter measured what tool surfaces cost in context: same GitHub task took 59,417 input tokens via MCP, 3,315 via a skill, 1,421 via the gh CLI
items.subheader: The GitHub MCP server's 46 default tool definitions alone add 19,436 tokens to every request on Sonnet 5.5, and one release-object result cost ~20,400 more. Tool Search cut the up-front cost under 600 tokens - halving the total on Sonnet 5.5, though it raised costs on Haiku 5.5.
items.image_alt: OpenRouter post card: MCP vs CLI vs Skills token costs

items.title: A2UI hits 1.0: an open protocol for agents to answer with generated native UI, with renderer SDKs for web, Android and iOS
items.subheader: Agent SDKs ship for Python, TypeScript and Dart; apps draw interfaces with native components securely, whether the agent lives in its own app or inside a third-party assistant hosting MCP apps.

items.title: United moves to block AI agents from its platforms, citing credential security and liability around tasks like check-in
items.subheader: The restrictions cut against the grain: Expedia and Booking are partnering with agents instead. A live fight over whether travel opens up to agent traffic or walls it off.

items.title: Lurie and City Administrator Chu use their new Prop. E powers for the first time: one citywide rulebook for $6 billion a year in contracting
items.subheader: The standards ban sharing confidential info with favored vendors, require conflict-of-interest disclosures, route contractor contact through official channels, and block splitting purchases to dodge competitive bidding. Rules take effect automatically after 60 days unless the mayor or a majority of supervisors blocks them.
items.image_alt: Carmen Chu and Daniel Lurie at Tuesday's press conference

quotes.text: Every day, dedicated public servants make decisions about how San Francisco spends taxpayer dollars. They deserve clear rules, practical guidance, and the confidence to speak up when something doesn't seem right.

items.title: Supervisors vote unanimously to legalize home restaurants: MEHKO permits let residents sell home-cooked food from their kitchens, carts or stalls
items.subheader: Permits cost $828 a year with a health inspection; home operations are capped at 90 meals a week and $100,000 in annual sales (200 and $200,000 for pushcarts). The vote follows a commissary-kitchen requirement vendors said priced them out at ~$1,000 a month.
items.image_alt: Fruit vendors on Mission Street (file photo)

quotes.text: This legislation will help break down barriers for aspiring food entrepreneurs, expand economic opportunities for immigrant-owned businesses and street vendors, and preserve the diverse culinary traditions that make San Francisco so special.

items.title: Heads up for the weekend: no BART trains between 24th Street and Daly City on Saturday and Sunday - free buses instead
items.subheader: Samtrans and Muni buses bridge the gap all weekend while crews install new train-control equipment, with some buses stopping at Glen Park and Balboa Park. Regular service resumes Monday at 5 a.m.
items.image_alt: 24th Street Mission BART station with a weekend service-change sign

items.title: SF weighs bringing back the 90-day shelter-stay cap, ending the unlimited stays that began in the pandemic - 383 people are on the wait list
items.subheader: Public comment closed Monday; the policy would take effect in March. Advocates worry extension rules put the burden on residents with uneven case-manager access - one client spent three days on the street mid-appeal and lost his documents. The city had 4,844 shelter beds at 91% occupancy at the end of 2025.

quotes.text: Shelter should be more than a safe place to sleep - it should be a pathway to stability and housing.
quotes.by: Dept. of Homelessness and Supportive Housing statement
